prompt.brief: Design a streaming analytics platform that ingests events from many sources, evaluates windowed patterns, maintains low-latency projections, and triggers reliable downstream actions.
successSignals: Define event contracts, partition keys, watermarks, windows, joins, state retention, trigger semantics, and delivery guarantees.
Partition streams by workload/key, isolate hot keys, handle late/duplicate/out-of-order events, and make state checkpoints/replay explicit.
Separate durable ingestion from stream operators, materialized views, action sinks, exploratory queries, and batch backfills.
Explain schema evolution, backpressure, poison events, exactly-once effects, observability, and degraded projections.

functional: Register sources and schemas, ingest events, run windowed SQL/pattern operators, publish aggregates, and trigger idempotent actions.
Expose job health, lag/watermarks, query results, pattern matches, output freshness, replay controls, and tenant usage.
Support reprocessing, schema versions, deletion/tombstones, dead-letter handling, checkpoint restore, and sink reconciliation.
nonFunctional: Publish standard window results and actions within five seconds while exposing lag and incomplete-window state.
Process 1M events per second across thousands of jobs without a single hot key or unbounded synchronous work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: 1M events/second, 10k streaming jobs, and 100k action sinks
Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

metrics.label: Peak scale
metrics.description: Capacity assumption that drives partitioning and backpressure.

metrics.description: User-facing budget for the primary request or read path.

metrics.label: Durable boundary
metrics.description: Accepted events and operator/checkpoint definitions are authoritative; views and actions are derived effects.

metrics.label: Async boundary
metrics.description: Keep Event Hubs for event ingestion, Stream Analytics for processing, Cosmos DB for output storage off the synchronous path.

dataFlow.title: Accept Ingest events from multiple sources
dataFlow.description: The Streaming analytics platform gateway authenticates the caller, validates the request, applies tenant policy and idempotency, then routes it to the owning service.

dataFlow.title: Commit the durable state
dataFlow.description: The service validates authorization and idempotency, then records the command before acknowledging the client.

dataFlow.title: Publish the domain event
dataFlow.description: A durable outbox publishes committed Streaming analytics platform events; consumers deduplicate by event ID and track offsets.

dataFlow.title: Build the read model
dataFlow.description: Partitioned workers consume Streaming analytics platform events, update the serving projection, and expose lag or watermark metadata.

dataFlow.title: Serve and recover asynchronously
dataFlow.description: Serving reads use the Streaming analytics platform projection; replay, repair, export, and slow work remain off the request path.

architecture.title: Design a real-time analytics solution that ingests millions of events, processes streaming data, detects patterns, and triggers actions based on analytics. reference architecture
architecture.summary: The authoritative state records Ingest events from multiple sources; asynchronous workers build serving projections while Event Hubs for event ingestion, Stream Analytics for processing, Cosmos DB for output storage stays isolated from the request path.

layers.label: Streaming analytics platform operations

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the accepted domain mutation strongly consistent; make derived projections explicitly eventually consistent.
Use idempotency keys, conditional writes, event IDs, and resource versions so retries are safe.
Return version and observedAt so clients can reason about projection freshness and convergence.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Streaming analytics platform by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Streaming analytics platform work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Streaming analytics platform projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable projection or a domain-safe degraded response when asynchronous dependencies fail.
Retain durable Streaming analytics platform records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure domain latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and source-to-projection correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.

rubric.description: The answer defines the primary workflow, data model, scale, latency, durability, and failure contract.
Entities and keys support the primary access patterns, authorization, privacy, and lifecycle changes.
Partitioning, cache behavior, queues, backpressure, and hot-key handling are explicit.
Idempotency, replay, recovery, degraded reads, and observability protect committed state.
The candidate can explain Streaming analytics platform consistency, push/pull, managed services, and the scale boundary.
